segments.text: What if your software engineers stopped writing most of the code themselves?
Software was never just code. Planning, testing, reviewing, shipping. Each step adds time, turning a simple idea into a twenty-day cycle. The bottleneck wasn't effort. It was the process.

So Coinbase changed the workflow. More than twenty-four hundred developers adopted Cursor, directing agents through implementation, testing, and review. The engineer moved up a level: define intent, validate results.
In Coinbase's reported workflow, agents created three out of every four pull requests. Not a side experiment. The new default.
Some teams cut the time from idea to production from twenty days to less than two. A ninety percent reduction. Not by typing faster, by removing handoffs.
The results weren't just about speed. Engineers merged fifty-five percent more pull requests, and saved seven hours every week. Small teams started shipping what once took a full team.
The biggest shift may not be how fast we write code, but how well we direct and review what AI builds. The next era is already here.
